title: USD alumni continue to support students through campus roles and traditions
text:
USD alumni continue to support students through campus roles and traditions
The University of South Dakota community continues to benefit from the ongoing involvement of its alumni, who support students by mentoring, contributing to scholarship funds, sharing their experiences, and participating in university traditions, according to a July 8 article on the university's website.
A commonly shared saying among graduates is: “Once a Yote, always a Yote.” For those alumni who have returned as employees at USD, this sense of pride translates into daily action. The article highlights five such individuals: Kyle Schoenfelder ’15, ’11, senior academic advisor in the Beacom School of Business; Kari Oyen, Ph.D. ’17, Ed.S ’08, program director and associate professor in school psychology and faculty athletic representative; Bryant Jackson, Ed.D. ’23, chief of police and adjunct instructor in educational leadership and criminal justice; Marcus Destin ’23, assistant director of student activities and multicultural affairs; and Cheryl Hartman, Ph.D., M.A. ’97, senior lecturer at USD – Sioux Falls and coordinator for the sociology program.
These alumni are recognized for their continued commitment to supporting current students throughout their careers at USD. Their contributions range from advising students academically to fostering diversity initiatives on campus.
The university also features several departments that promote student engagement with broader social issues. The Department of Sustainability and Environment enables students to address environmental and social challenges through actions on campus or within the Vermillion community or along the Missouri River. It operates within the College of Arts and Sciences at USD using the Akeley-Lawrence Science Center as its main facility. The department inspires participants to consider ideal world conditions while strategizing positive change efforts. It stands as the only university department in its region offering both undergraduate and graduate degrees in sustainability programs while extending influence through partnerships such as with the Missouri River Institute along the Missouri National Recreational River, according to information provided by the official website.
The highlighted alumni demonstrate how tradition combines with active engagement across academic programs at USD.
